news.title: Intercom tests a $19 seat while the rest of the market shows its prices: 15 reveals in a week of quiet cuts
news.gist: PricingSaaS’s review of 28 Sep–4 Oct describes a busier-than-usual week: price reveals and promotions ran at about twice their norm, cuts beat their average, and Intercom’s cheaper seat turned out to be a test.
points: Slack moved Enterprise+ from contact sales to a listed per-user price, and Datadog published Kafka Console pricing per broker host
The review reads n8n’s and Synthesia’s smaller allowances as price rises made through credits rather than through list prices
MindsDB and fal raised inference and GPU rates again, and the review says a third rise would make it a trend
Psychz Networks had the week’s biggest hike, and OpenAI’s cached-input cut on GPT-6.1 Sol was the biggest cut
nums: changes logged in the week
eight-week average of weekly changes
price cuts, against a 6.8 average
price reveals, against a normal 6.8
promotions, against a 19.6 average
news.why: With reveals and promotions both running high, a quote from last month may now be beaten by a listed price or an offer, so check again before you renew.

news.title: Intercom hikes Essential seat price back to $29 five days after cutting it to $19
news.gist: Intercom’s Essential seat seemed to bounce from $19 back to $29, but fresh browser sessions and the page code show a live experiment that assigns each visitor a price on their first visit.
points: The page source names a seat-price-reduction experiment with control and treatment arms, and a second experiment runs on Pro pricing
Advanced and Expert seat prices were identical in every session
Anyone who signed at the lower price should check whether their annual contract keeps it at renewal
This price point moved three times in five weeks, far faster than Intercom’s usual rhythm
nums: Essential seat price shown to the test group
Essential seat price on annual billing shown to most visitors
size of the move back up to $29
63 days
Intercom’s typical gap between pricing changes
news.why: If a vendor’s page shows you a lower seat price than a colleague saw, get it in writing and ask what renewal will cost.

news.title: fal raises serverless H100 rate to $2.49/hr, adds GB200 GPU, doubles MiniMax video pricing
news.gist: fal raised serverless rates on two heavily used GPU tiers, added Nvidia’s GB200 and doubled a video model’s per-second rate, and the article asks whether this starts a broader repricing of fal’s catalog.
points: It is fal’s third real pricing change since tracking began in late July, and its second GPU rate rise
Developers building on fal now have to absorb the higher cost or pass it on to their own customers
The article reads the GB200 launch as fal keeping pace with new hardware while earning more from its older fleet
Most of the other late-September rises it lists, at Shipday, Cumul and Hedra, were seat prices rather than compute
nums: new hourly H100 serverless rate, up from $1.89
rise in the H100 rate
rise in the B300 rate, to $5.99 an hour
new per-second MiniMax H3 Max rate, double the old $0.025
news.why: If an AI tool you buy runs on rented GPUs, expect rises like these to reach you later as dearer credits or smaller allowances.

news.title: Monetizing Credit Flexibility
news.gist: Credit-based plans let vendors steer upgrades, annual commitments and usage by changing when credits arrive, how long they last and what spends them, all without touching list prices.
points: Runway lets unused monthly credits roll over for a month only on Max, which gives heavy users with uneven workloads a reason to move up
Framer adds bonus first-month credits on yearly Basic and Pro, and switching to monthly billing removes the bonus
Replit’s Free Mode lets paying users chat on a cheaper model without spending credits, and Lovable’s daily grants work in a similar way
Litterst’s advice is to choose the behavior you want first, then write the credit rules around it
nums: credits in the first month on Framer’s yearly Basic and Pro plans
Supabase’s new metered log ingestion rate after 20 GB on Pro and Team
users Devin’s Team plan now allows, down from unlimited
news.why: Credit rules such as rollovers, bonuses and expiry change what a plan is really worth, so compare them as carefully as the price.

news.title: The Agent P&L Framework (with Manu Mehra, Strategic Pricing at Databricks)
news.gist: Per-token billing suits model makers and outcome pricing suits the few vendors with clean attribution; everyone else should price agents between a cost floor and a value ceiling and show buyers what each successful result costs.
points: Mehra gives each agent a P&L: infrastructure, inference, evals and governance on the cost side; revenue, hours saved and errors avoided on the value side
The piece argues that credits explain how to bill but not what to charge or why the price sits above token costs
In PricingSaaS’s own testing, accuracy and rework is the biggest difference between good and frustrating agents
The roundup notes Slack A/B testing a public Enterprise+ price and Retool dropping its Enterprise AI credit offer
nums: share of an analyst’s SQL an agent writes in Mehra’s productivity example
changes the newsletter observed in its weekly roundup
$45/user/month
Enterprise+ price Slack is testing in public
AI credit cut n8n made when it rebranded them as Assistant credits
news.why: When a vendor pitches an agent, ask for its cost per successful outcome rather than its credit price to judge whether it pays for itself.

news.title: Developer Tool Pricing Changes: September 28–October 4, 2026
news.gist: AgentDeals’ digest for the week is dominated by shrinking sign-up credits and shutdowns, plus infrastructure vendors billing separately for things that used to be included in instance prices.
points: Browser Use and Exa cut their sign-up credits, while Neon and TraceLog raised free allowances
Pipedream stopped new Workflows sign-ups, and Solo is shutting down and deleting all sites with no recovery
Fly.io raised its machine memory price, so every preset costs more even though CPU prices are unchanged
Meta resumed charging for WhatsApp service messages once a number’s free monthly allowance runs out
nums: Browser Use’s one-time sign-up credit, down from $15
rise in OVHcloud Gen3 total bills from separate storage and IPv4 charges
Modal’s new egress charge per GiB beyond the included allowance
free WhatsApp service messages per business phone number a month
news.why: Read infrastructure bills line by line after October, because new storage, IP and egress charges can raise the total while the headline rate stays the same.

patterns.t: AI compute costs reached the price list
patterns.p: Rises in GPU and model rates showed up straight away in what AI apps charge: more credits per video, smaller included caps, per-model meters. Buyers of AI media and agent tools feel the supplier’s costs within weeks.

points.text: raised every serverless GPU rate again, H100 from $1.89 to $2.49 an hour, and doubled MiniMax video pricing
raised DeepSeek V4.1 Flash rates from $0.22/$0.66 to $0.30/$1.20 per million tokens and ended its credit-match promo
roughly doubled Seedance 2.0 video-to-video credit costs, to 30–314 credits a second

halved included AI video caps on every plan, Core from 500 to 250, with credits unchanged
moved its AI SRE add-on from a flat $5 per million tokens to per-model pricing

patterns.p: Vendors cut free credits, caps and features, sometimes while enlarging paid plans, so the free tier works as a trial rather than a home. Three of the eight come from PricingSaaS reports.

patterns.t: More included at the same price
patterns.p: At the other end, vendors raised quotas, seats and credits without changing prices, a cheap way to win share in crowded categories. Half of these come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: More changes cost buyers more than saved them money
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that cost buyers more vs less; the other 46 repackage
stats_analysis.p: The rises ran from Baremetrics’ new fixed tiers and fal’s GPU rates to Xero and CROSStrax lifting every plan, plus n8n’s smaller AI allowance. The savings were led by OpenAI’s cached-input cut, Logz.io’s cheaper metrics for new plans and 7shifts’ lower Premium price. Many of the week’s records, including Xero, CROSStrax and 7shifts, come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: A third of the week involved AI
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that touch AI features or AI pricing
stats_analysis.p: AI changes ran both ways. OpenAI and Cohere cut model prices while fal and MindsDB raised theirs; Salesforce and Moz enlarged AI allowances while n8n and Synthesia shrank them. LangChain changed the unit its AI compute is billed in.

stats_analysis.t: Limits loosened about as often as they tightened
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that loosen vs tighten a limit
stats_analysis.p: Loosening came as bigger quotas at the same price, from Moz and Ideogram to Airtable’s automations and G2’s unlimited users. Tightening hit compute and AI caps: Render halved its largest Workflows instance and Artlist halved AI video caps, while SimScale and HiveMQ cut free allowances. Many of the smaller moves come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: Straight price cuts edged out straight increases
stats_analysis.p: Counted by list price alone, cuts slightly outnumbered rises, but two of the cuts come with catches: Intercom’s cheaper seat is a test, and InVideo’s cheaper seats came with dearer video credits. The increases were broader, with Xero, Jungleworks and CROSStrax raising every plan.

stats_analysis.t: Free plans were a busy lever
stats_analysis.figNote: changes aimed at the free plan
stats_analysis.p: Synthesia, Strawberry Browser, Plytix and SimScale gave free users less, while Neon, Invoice Ninja and ToolJet gave them more and Beyond Pricing and Balena added free plans. Most of the free-plan moves come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: The top of the list leans toward higher costs
stats_analysis.p: Of the 21, 9 cost buyers more, 5 save them money and 7 repackage. The rises include Baremetrics, beehiiv, fal and Xero; the savings are led by OpenAI and Cohere, plus Airtable reversing its own new cap.

news_trends.t: AI compute costs are rising and being passed on
news_trends.p: PricingSaaS flagged repeat rate rises at fal and MindsDB, and the developer digest shows infrastructure bills climbing through new line items at OVHcloud, Fly.io and Modal. Our records show the knock-on effect: Luma and InVideo now charge more credits per Seedance video.

news_trends.t: Credits became the main pricing lever
news_trends.p: Litterst’s two essays treat credits as a way to steer behavior and as a billing layer that still needs a value story, and the weekly review read n8n’s and Synthesia’s smaller allowances as quiet price rises. Our records show credits moving both ways, more at Salesforce and Ideogram, fewer at n8n and on Synthesia’s free plan.
